title: Core Concurrency Terminology: Race Condition, Critical Section, Mutex
prompt:
Give me the difference between these three in one sentence each:
1. Race condition
2. Critical section
3. Mutex

forbidden_misconceptions: critical section is an error or bug
race condition requires different processes only
evaluator_rubric.scoring_criteria: Learner must define: (1) Race condition as bug where output depends on timing/interleaving of concurrent access to shared state; (2) Critical section as code segment accessing shared resources that requires exclusive access; (3) Mutex as mutual exclusion synchronization mechanism enforcing single-thread execution in critical section.
evaluator_rubric.ideal_response_summary: A race condition occurs when concurrent threads access shared data and the final outcome depends on the non-deterministic timing of their execution. A critical section is a sequence of code accessing shared resources that must not be executed concurrently by more than one thread. A mutex is a mutual exclusion locking primitive used to ensure that only one thread can execute a critical section at any given time.
